texts.preamble: Ahmed Khan Alias Ahamed vs Prakash Dewasi on 20 May, 2025 Kabc020344502022 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Court Of Small Causes, At Bengaluru. (Scch-25) - : Present:- Smt. Prakriti Kalyanpur, B.A(L),Ll.B., Ll.M. Xxiii Additional Small Causes Judge, Bengaluru. Dated This The 20Th Day Of May 2025 Mvc No.6418/2022 Petitioner: Mr. Ahmed Khan @ Ahamed S/o. Pyare Jan, Aged about 31 years, Resident of Mindahalli, Tayalur, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District.
texts.facts: The case of the Petitioner in brief is that: On 14.08.2022 between 7.45 and 8.00pm, when the Petitioner was riding Bajaj C.T.100 motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-ES-7772 from Mulabagal towards his native place i.e., Mindahalli and he came near Attikunte Village, a TVS Jupiter two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-08-X-1885 came on the said Road in the opposite direction i.e., from KGF side in high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle. Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down on the road. At that point of time a Truck came from the back side of the petitioner's vehicle and ran over the left leg of the petitioner. As such, petitioner suffered grievous injuries. 3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Mulabagal. After first aid treatment he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital and Research Centre, Tamaka, Kolar wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 15.08.2022 to 01.09.2022, underwent surgery to the above knee amputation of left lower limb under GA and wound debridement + Stay suturing muscle coverage on 18.08.2022 under GA and discharged with advice for further surgery and bed rest. So far he has spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards conveyance, food and nourishment and medicines. Prior to the date of accident the petitioner was a Painter by profession and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. Due to the unfortunate accident and amputation of left lower limb, petitioner is unable to walk, sit, squat, climb stairs or do any work as he was doing prior to the accident. The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the TVS Jupiter Two Wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-08- X-1885. The Mulabagal Rural Police have registered a case in their Cr.No.184/2022 p/u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC. The 1 st Respondent being the Owner and the 2 nd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, this petition. 4. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements. Ahmed Khan Alias Ahamed vs Prakash Dewasi on 20 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52056152/ 2 5. The objections of the Respondent No.1: He has denied the entire petition averments except admitting the ownership of the vehicle bearing No.KA-08-X- 1885 and submits that the vehicle has valid policy as on the date of accident. Further admitted that he was driving the vehicle having a valid license as on the date of accident. Further contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the petitioner himself. There is no negligence on his part. Petitioner was under the influence of alcohol while driving the vehicle. He has denied the manner of accident. He has also denied the petitioner's avocation, income and medical expenses. Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant. Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition. 6. The objections of the Respondent No.2: It has denied the entire petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the insured Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-X-1885 in favour of the 1 st respondent. Further submitted that the petition has been filed on 23.11.2022 and the alleged accident occurred on 14.08.2022. Thus this petition is barred by limitation under Sec.166 (3) of MV (Amendment) Act 2019. The rider of the offending motorcycle did not have valid DL as on the date of accident. The 1st respondent has allowed a person who was not having valid and effective DL to drive the same as on the date of accident. There is non compliance of Sec.158(6) of MV Act. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner.
texts.arguments: Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive. The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decisions: 1.ILR 2009 KAR 3562 : Veerappa and Anr. Vs. Siddappa and Anr. 2. The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decisions: 1.ILR 2009 KAR 3562 : Veerappa and Anr. Vs. Siddappa and Anr. Once the insured plays fraud, admits liability with the sole object of foisting liability on the insurance company, though in fact he knew that it is not true, liability of the insurance company to indemnify such insured ceases. 2. MFA No.7018/2023 C/w MFA No.2658/2024 : M/s TATA AIG Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Sri. Manjunatha and Ors. Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that, in case of the driver having no DL at all, the liability has to be fastened on the owner of the offending vehicle. Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, 'if the insurance companies are saddled with the burden of challenging the charge sheets filed throughout the country without there being no clear legal mandate'. 20.
